what_it_does: Modern chips pack CPUs, GPUs, and specialized neural network processors (NPUs) together on one die. To prevent one component from corrupting another's memory, chips use hardware memory protection—essentially cryptographic checksums over memory regions. The problem: this protection uses fixed granularity (all regions protected the same way), but CPUs access memory in fine, structured patterns while GPUs and NPUs access in coarse, random patterns. Conventional protection tuned for CPUs creates excessive overhead on GPUs. This work proposes multi-granular protection: the same chip dynamically adjusts whether each region uses coarse-grained or fine-grained protection based on actual access patterns observed from each processor, using a smart tree structure that stores protection metadata at multiple levels to reduce redundant checks.
